definition: The use of a cipher and a key to scramble readable data into ciphertext so that only someone holding the right key can turn it back and read it.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 4: Protocols

definition: The system of certificate authorities, digital certificates, and policies that binds public keys to verified identities so parties on untrusted networks can exchange data securely.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 4: Protocols

definition: A digitally signed electronic file that ties a public key to the verified identity of a user, device, or website and is issued by a trusted authority.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 4: Protocols

definition: A trusted public or private entity that verifies identities and then issues, signs, maintains, and revokes the digital certificates used in a PKI.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 4: Protocols

definition: A certificate signed with its creator's own private key instead of a trusted third party; fine for labs and internal tests, but browsers distrust it and it cannot be revoked.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 4: Protocols

definition: The process of controlling every stage of a cryptographic key's life cycle: generation, distribution, secure storage, rotation, revocation, and destruction.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 4: Protocols

definition: Information while it moves across a network or the Internet, its most exposed state, protected with secure protocols such as TLS, SSH, or a VPN.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 9: Network Security

definition: Information stored on a nonvolatile medium such as a drive or backup, protected with storage encryption, access controls, and data loss prevention tools.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 9: Network Security

definition: The requirement to store and process data only inside specific countries or regions so that it complies with local privacy laws and contracts, checked during audits.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 9: Network Security

term: Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard
definition: Industry security standard that every organization that stores, processes, or transmits credit card information must follow to reduce fraud and protect cardholders.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 9: Network Security

definition: European Union law that protects the personal data and privacy of people in the EU and sets strict rules for how organizations collect and handle it.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 9: Network Security

definition: The process of verifying that a user, device, or application is who or what it claims to be, for example by checking a username and password.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 11: Access Control

definition: Login method that requires proofs from at least two different categories, such as something you know, have, are, or do, or somewhere you are.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 11: Access Control

definition: Login method that requires a generated code, such as one from an authenticator app or hardware fob, that stays valid for only a short period like 30 seconds.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 11: Access Control

definition: Security method that uses a device's GPS, Wi-Fi, cellular, or IP-based location to allow or deny access depending on whether it is inside a defined virtual boundary.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 9: Network Security

definition: Framework of policies, processes, and tools that manages digital identities across their life cycle and controls which resources each user or device may reach.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 9: Network Security

definition: Login method in which a user proves identity once and then reaches many systems or applications without entering credentials again; one stolen login therefore opens many resources.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 11: Access Control

definition: Service that stores user credentials and performs authentication for other websites and apps, which trust its assertion instead of handling passwords themselves.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 11: Access Control

definition: XML-based open standard that passes authentication and authorization assertions from an identity provider to a service provider, commonly used for web-based single sign-on.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 9: Network Security

definition: Open-standard AAA protocol that centralizes login for remote, VPN, and wireless clients; it normally uses UDP, combines authentication with authorization, and encrypts only the password.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 11: Access Control

term: Terminal Access Controller Access Control System Plus
definition: Cisco-developed AAA protocol on TCP port 49 that encrypts the whole exchange, separates authentication, authorization, and accounting, and mainly controls router and switch administration.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 11: Access Control

definition: Access model in which permissions are assigned to job functions, and each user receives the rights of the job group the administrator places them in.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 9: Network Security

definition: Strictest access model, in which the system compares sensitivity labels on users and objects, such as secret or top secret, and only administrators set the rules.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 9: Network Security

definition: Access model in which the owner of a file, folder, or printer decides who may use it, with each user's rights stored in that object's permission list.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 9: Network Security

definition: Video device placed at entrances, data rooms, and other secure areas, often feeding a CCTV system, to record or watch activity and help investigate intrusions.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 11: Access Control

definition: Door lock opened by entering a code on a keypad, which avoids lost keys and can log entries, schedule access times, and raise a duress alarm.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 11: Access Control

definition: Small space between two locking doors where the first must close before the second opens, so only one or two people can enter at a time.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 11: Access Control

definition: Single decoy server that looks real and slightly vulnerable, with tempting fake data, used to lure attackers away from production systems and study their methods.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 9: Network Security

definition: Entire decoy network of several monitored lure systems that tracks all attacker traffic in and out, giving a fuller picture of attack methods than one host.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 9: Network Security

definition: The likelihood that a weakness will be taken advantage of, weighed together with the harm that would result.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 10: Risk Management

definition: A weakness in a system, process, or design, such as an unpatched service or an open port, that could allow unauthorized access.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 10: Risk Management

definition: The act or the code that takes advantage of a weakness in a system to gain unauthorized access or cause harm.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 10: Risk Management

definition: Anything, such as an attacker, malware, or a disaster, that has the potential to cause harm to systems or data.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 10: Risk Management

definition: Security principle that only authorized users or the intended recipient can view data, supported by encryption, passwords, and access controls.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 4: Protocols

definition: Security principle that data is not changed without authorization between sender and receiver, supported by hashing and digital signatures.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 4: Protocols

definition: Security principle that systems and data stay reachable by authorized users whenever needed, supported by backups, redundancy, and disaster recovery.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 4: Protocols

definition: The three-part security model whose goals are keeping data private, unaltered, and accessible to authorized users; every security control supports one or more of them.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 4: Protocols

definition: Everyday network-connected devices such as cameras, thermostats, and sensors, which should be isolated in their own VLAN or segment because many are hard to secure and patch.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 9: Network Security

definition: Industrial sensors and controllers in factories and utilities that are exposed to the Internet, using a decentralized design to collect large amounts of operational data.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 8: Network Segmentation

definition: Centralized system that monitors and controls widespread processes such as utilities or traffic signals through an operator interface; best kept physically separate from the corporate LAN.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 8: Network Segmentation

definition: Hardware and software, such as programmable logic controllers and remote terminal units, that gather real-time data from physical machinery and control industrial processes.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 9: Network Security

definition: Hardware and software that directly monitors and controls physical infrastructure, where a breach risks physical damage rather than only lost data or services.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 8: Network Segmentation

definition: Policy that lets employees use their personal phones, tablets, and laptops for work, which requires segmenting those devices away from sensitive corporate resources.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 11: Access Control

definition: Software that enrolls phones and tablets and enforces passwords, encryption, remote wipe, and other policies on them, often used to support personal devices at work.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 11: Access Control

definition: Attack from a single source that floods a system or network with more traffic or requests than it can handle, so legitimate users cannot reach it.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 9: Network Security

definition: Flooding attack launched at once from many compromised machines, usually a botnet under a command-and-control server, which makes it far harder to block than a single source.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 9: Network Security

definition: Group of malware-infected computers and IoT devices, remotely directed by a command-and-control server without the owners knowing, often used to launch flooding attacks.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 10: Risk Management

definition: Attack that spoofs the victim's IP address in small requests to many public UDP servers such as DNS or NTP, so their larger replies all flood the victim.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 10: Risk Management

definition: Attack that sends many TCP connection requests but never completes the three-way handshake, filling the server with half-open connections until it refuses legitimate ones.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 9: Network Security

definition: Wireless attack that sends spoofed management frames telling clients and the access point to end their session, knocking users off Wi-Fi, often to push them to a rogue AP.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 10: Risk Management

definition: General attack in which a host on one VLAN gets its frames into a different, restricted VLAN, for example by stacking tags or by posing as a trunk.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 8: Network Segmentation

definition: VLAN attack that puts two 802.1Q tags on a frame, so after the first switch strips the outer tag, the hidden inner tag delivers it to a restricted VLAN.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 8: Network Segmentation

definition: VLAN attack in which the attacker's device negotiates a trunk link with a switch port, so it can then send and receive traffic for every VLAN.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 8: Network Segmentation

definition: Attack that fills a switch's MAC address table with fake source addresses until it fails open and sends every frame out all ports, like a hub.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 7: Network Architecture

definition: Attack that keeps sending false replies to corrupt the stored IP-to-MAC cache of targeted hosts, so traffic meant for a legitimate IP address goes to the attacker.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 9: Network Security

definition: Attack that sends forged ARP messages claiming a legitimate host's MAC-to-IP mapping, letting the attacker impersonate that host, get past allow lists, or intercept its traffic.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 9: Network Security

definition: Unauthorized address server on a LAN that gives clients false settings, such as the attacker's IP as default gateway or DNS server, to enable on-path attacks.
acceptedAnswers: Rogue Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol server
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 10: Risk Management

definition: Attack that injects false records into a name server's cache so that lookups resolve to the attacker's IP address and users are sent to fake sites.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 9: Network Security

definition: Broad term for any technique that forges or manipulates name resolution replies, including cache tampering, hijacking, and interception, to redirect traffic to malicious destinations.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 9: Network Security

definition: Wireless device plugged into the network without the administrator's knowledge, which usually ignores security policy and opens a back door for attackers.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 9: Network Security

definition: Fake wireless access point that copies a legitimate network's SSID and settings so users connect to it and the attacker can capture their traffic.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 6: Wireless Networking

definition: Attack in which the intruder secretly sits between two communicating devices to capture, read, or alter their traffic before passing it on.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 9: Network Security

definition: Manipulating people, rather than technology, into revealing passwords or other sensitive information or granting access; defended mainly by user training.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 10: Risk Management

definition: Fraudulent email, website, or call that pretends to come from a trusted source to trick victims into giving credentials or financial details.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 10: Risk Management

definition: Searching through an organization's discarded papers and trash for passwords or other useful information, prevented by proper shredding.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 10: Risk Management

definition: Secretly watching someone type a password, PIN, or door code, or read their screen, to steal that information.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 10: Risk Management

definition: Following an authorized person closely through a secure door before it closes, without that person's knowledge or consent.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 10: Risk Management

definition: Getting into a secure area with an authorized person's cooperation, for example by posing as a delivery worker and asking them to hold the door.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 10: Risk Management

definition: Any software or code written to harm, disrupt, or gain unauthorized access to a system, including viruses, worms, Trojans, bots, and ransomware.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 10: Risk Management

definition: Malicious program that locks or encrypts a victim's system or data and demands payment to restore it; offline backups are the main defense.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 10: Risk Management

definition: Malicious program disguised as useful or harmless software that does not replicate itself but delivers a harmful payload once installed.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 10: Risk Management

definition: Malicious program that runs on its own and spreads between computers across a network without needing to attach to another file.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 10: Risk Management

definition: Hidden malicious code that stays dormant until a set condition or date occurs and then performs its harmful action.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 9: Network Security

definition: Reducing a device's attack surface by patching it, disabling unneeded ports and services, changing default credentials, and using secure protocols.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 9: Network Security

definition: Hardening step that shuts down switch interfaces and closes TCP and UDP ports that nothing needs, so attackers cannot plug in or connect through them.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 7: Network Architecture

definition: Hardening step that stops software processes a server or device does not need, such as Telnet or FTP, removing extra ways in for attackers.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 10: Risk Management

definition: Vendor-set login, often admin with a simple value like 1234, shipped on routers and other devices; attackers know it, so change it before use.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 10: Risk Management

definition: Switch feature that drops address offers arriving on untrusted ports to block rogue servers and builds a binding table of legitimate IP-to-MAC pairs.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 10: Risk Management

definition: Switch feature that checks ARP messages against the DHCP snooping binding table and drops those whose IP and MAC addresses do not match.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 10: Risk Management

definition: Method that checks a device's identity and security posture, such as antivirus status, before letting it on the network, and can quarantine devices that fail.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 9: Network Security

definition: IEEE 802.1X standard in which a switch or access point passes a connecting device's EAP credentials to an authentication server, often RADIUS, before opening the port.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 9: Network Security

definition: Allow or deny list of hardware addresses that an access point or switch uses to admit only approved devices; easy to defeat by spoofing an address.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 9: Network Security

definition: Switch feature that limits which and how many source MAC addresses may use an access port, and shuts down or restricts the port on a violation.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 7: Network Architecture

definition: Ordered list of permit and deny rules on a router, switch, or firewall that filters traffic by criteria such as IP address, port, or protocol.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 9: Network Security

definition: Security rule that allows or blocks web requests by matching their addresses or site categories against a local or cloud database of websites.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 9: Network Security

definition: Security rule that inspects the actual data in web pages, email, or files and blocks malware, spam, inappropriate material, or leaks of sensitive information.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 9: Network Security

definition: Rule at the end of an ACL or firewall policy that blocks any traffic not specifically permitted by an earlier rule.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 9: Network Security

definition: Network area under the organization's control, such as the internal LAN, where firewalls and ACLs apply the strictest filtering and hosts reach the Internet only through a proxy.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 8: Network Segmentation

definition: Network area outside the organization's control, such as the Internet or public Wi-Fi, whose incoming traffic is heavily filtered or blocked.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 8: Network Segmentation

definition: Perimeter segment between an outer and an inner firewall that holds public-facing servers, reachable from the Internet but kept apart from the internal LAN.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 8: Network Segmentation
